Modafinil (ATC code N06BA07) is a medication used in the treatment of ADHD. In the context of the Danish national ADHD database quality monitoring, it is recognized as one of six specific ADHD medications included in the calculation of [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]], which measures pharmacological treatment coverage among ADHD patients in standardized care pathways [^src1] [^src2]. It serves as an alternative treatment under specific clinical conditions [^src1]. 

In the 2024 annual report, the scope of the database was expanded to include adults, introducing [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] for pharmacological treatment among adults with ADHD [^src3]. Modafinil is explicitly listed as one of the medication types included in the calculation for this new indicator, alongside dexamphetamine, methylphenidate, atomoxetine, lisdexamphetamine, and guanfacine [^src3]. 

The inclusion of Modafinil in these indicators highlights its role in the systematic quality measurement of ADHD treatment in Denmark, where the ADHD database functions as central infrastructure for clinical quality development, political steering, and evidence-based practice [^src3]. The data also points to broader systemic discussions regarding regional variations in medical treatment practices, case-mix, resource pressure, and registration practices across Danish regions [^src1] [^src2] [^src3].
